newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sumitomo says no plans for physical copper retreat.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo says no plans for physical copper retreat.

text.p: Japan's Sumitomo Corp does not intend to withdraw from Asian physical copper markets, although it may not be as competitive on pricing as previously, the head of the trading company's Singapore operations told Reuters.

"It is not our intention to withdraw, but our approach might be slightly different...Our new offer prices may not be as competitive as before," Hisayoshi Uno, managing director of Sumitomo Corp Singapore Pte Ltd, said in a telephone interview.

Uno said the emphasis of Sumitomo's copper trading would now be on covered physical business rather than London Metal Exchange (LME) futures trading after the company's copper dealing debacle this year in which it lost $2.6 billion.

Japanese copper traders said that before Sumitomo's former chief copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka was fired in June for alleged illicit trades, the trade house sold copper at sizeable discounts to customers both domestically and abroad. They speculated he covered losses from the discounts with gains from futures trading on the LME.

Major copper end users in Thailand and Malaysia said on Tuesday that they believed Sumitomo was withdrawing from their refined copper markets because the company had given no indication of its supply intentions next year.
Uno said that Sumitomo's commitment to the physical copper market was evidenced by its minority stake in the $1.6 billion Batu Hijau gold and copper mining project in Indonesia.
"We would like to maintain our business...it depends on whether we can compete competitively," he said.
